elements.element: Preferred: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it, with Vendor assignment
elements.evidence: The insertion grants only a licence: "Licensor hereby grants to Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license"; no assignment of Custom Deliverables to Licensee.
"Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein."

elements.element: Preferred: perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license to use, modify and sublicense the Custom Deliverables"

elements.element: Preferred: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Licensee owns all right, title and interest in and to all data, orders, trade records and other information submitted, generated or derived by or on behalf of Licensee ... (\"Licensee Data\")"
No express no-joint-ownership statement; ownership is allocated solely to Licensor (platform) and Licensee (Licensee Data), but the concept is not stated.

"Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein" — Licensed Technology comprises Licensed Know-How and Licensed Software, and the insertion carves out nothing of Licensor's tooling.
Definition 1.9: "LICENSED TECHNOLOGY means the Licensed Know-How and the Licensed Software", coupled with "Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology".
"any customization, unique client front end or other development work performed by Licensor specifically for Licensee ... (the \"Custom Deliverables\")"
"perpetual"; "which license shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement"

reasons: The redline sits at the locked fallback: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Custom Deliverables for Licensee's business purposes, with Licensor's platform ownership (including Licensed Know-How and its tooling) untouched.

Preferred is not reached because there is no assignment of deliverables/work product to Licensee and no express 'no joint ownership' statement; these are noted, not redlined, given the fallback target.

Generic tools and know-how are not restated affirmatively in the insertion, but Vendor ownership of them survives in full through the untouched Article III ownership grant and the Licensed Technology definition, so the fallback's Vendor-side allocation is intact.

Minimal: a single 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' insertion after the ownership paragraph; the Licensee Data limb is needed only to stop Article III's sweeping ownership language capturing our own trade and order data, and no other sentence is rewritten.

Intent preserved: Article VII(b) change-order mechanic, Article XXI return and certification, and Licensor's survival language all remain effective, and the licence's express survival avoids a conflict with the automatic licence termination in Article XXI(a).

Optional tightening for the negotiation (not a deviation): the licence is limited to work 'paid for by Licensee', which is narrower than the playbook's deliverables scope and could be broadened to all work performed specifically for Licensee.
